U9.description: A separate wireless MCU for BLE and sub-GHz networking. Linux communicates with its firmware over UART6. Radio capabilities depend on the loaded firmware.
U9.name: Wireless microcontroller
U9.specification: SMD IC RF TxRx + MCU 2.4G & sub 1G ;VQFN-48

D2.description: SMD Diode Array ESD;4 Channel,6 Gbps,5.5V;USON-10
D2.name: Diode Array ESD

D1.description: SMD Diode Array ESD;4 Channel,6 Gbps,5.5V;USON-10
D1.name: Diode Array ESD

U1.description: Runs Linux and coordinates memory, storage, display, and peripheral interfaces. The chip contains four Cortex-A53 cores plus real-time processing subsystems.
U1.name: Application processor

U16.description: Generates the 1.0 V supply used by the single-pair Ethernet PHY from a 1.8 V input rail.
U16.name: 1.0 V regulator

U12.description: Efficient step-down supply for the main 3.3 V rail and expansion connectors. The PMIC controls its enable input.
U12.name: 3.3 V step-down converter
U12.specification: SMD IC PMIC;DCDC Buck-ADJ ,2.5-V to 5.5-V Input, 4-A;VSON-6

U17.description: TPS6521903 manages the board power sequence and generates several processor, memory and I/O supply rails. Its configuration interface connects to the local I²C bus.
U17.name: Power management IC

U13.description: Translates RMII data from the processor into 10BASE-T1L signaling over one twisted pair. The RJ11 port also provides a controlled power output.
U13.name: Single-pair Ethernet PHY
U13.specification: SMD IC 10Base-T1L 10M Single Pair Ethernet Transceiver;QFN32

U3.description: Soldered flash storage for the bootloader, Linux, and user files. Connected to the processor through its eight-bit MMC0 interface.
U3.name: 16 GB eMMC flash

U20.description: Stores board identification data on the local I²C0 bus. This small EEPROM is separate from the eMMC storage.
U20.name: Board ID EEPROM

U2.description: Working memory for the operating system and applications. Its dedicated parallel DDR bus carries address, command, clock, and data signals.
U2.name: 2 GB DDR4 RAM

U11.description: Converts two analog inputs into digital measurements using the ADC102S021. Its serial interface connects to the processor; the expansion inputs are separate channels.
U11.name: Two-channel 10-bit ADC

U7.description: Bridges the parallel RGB display bus to HDMI. I²C2 configures the chip, and McASP1 supplies digital audio.
U7.name: HDMI transmitter

U18.description: Keeps time independently of Linux. A backup coin cell can maintain the clock while main board power is off.
U18.name: Real-time clock

U6.description: Converts the processor’s RGMII interface into Ethernet signaling. The RJ45 connector includes magnetics between the PHY and the network cable.
U6.name: Gigabit Ethernet PHY

SW1.description: Connects to the power-management control path for board power operations. Behavior depends on press duration and the running software.
SW1.name: Power button

SW2.description: Requests a system reset. This is a separate control from powering off the board.
SW2.name: Reset button

SW3.description: Used for boot selection at startup and as a software input. The documentation describes holding it for SD-card boot selection.
SW3.name: User / boot button

U5.description: Dual-band Wi-Fi module connected through SDIO. Two external antenna sockets serve its radio paths. Bluetooth and sub-GHz functions are handled by the separate CC1352P7.
U5.name: Dual-band Wi-Fi module

J13.description: Connects peripherals such as keyboards, mice, and cameras to the USB1 host controller. A power switch feeds the port’s VBUS.
J13.name: USB-A host

J14.description: Supplies 5 V power and provides a USB device connection to a host computer. This connector does not negotiate higher USB-PD voltages.
J14.name: USB-C power & device

J4.description: Receives digital video from the IT66121 transmitter. The transmitter bridges the processor’s parallel display signals to HDMI.
J4.name: HDMI output

J6.description: UART0 console for boot messages and a Linux terminal using a compatible logic-level serial adapter. This is not an RS-232 voltage interface.
J6.name: Serial console

J8.description: Connects a compatible LVDS/OLDI display. Display lanes run directly to the processor; control and power circuits support the panel.
J8.name: Display ribbon connector

J17.description: Connects a compatible MIPI CSI-2 camera. Image data uses differential lanes, while a separate I²C link configures the camera.
J17.name: Camera ribbon connector

J1.description: Accepts a microSD card for booting, expanding storage, or installing an image to eMMC. Uses MMC1; it is a separate interface from onboard eMMC.
J1.name: microSD socket

J7.description: Expansion port exposing I²C1 with power and ground. Alternate functions depend on pin multiplexing and software configuration.
J7.name: Grove connector

J3.description: Coaxial antenna connection to the corresponding radio. The highlighted path includes the RF matching network as a functional group.
J3.name: Wi-Fi antenna 2

J5.description: Coaxial antenna connection to the corresponding radio. The highlighted path includes the RF matching network as a functional group.
J5.name: Wi-Fi antenna 1

J9.description: Coaxial antenna connection to the corresponding radio. The highlighted path includes the RF matching network as a functional group.
J9.name: 2.4 GHz antenna

J12.description: Coaxial antenna connection to the corresponding radio. The highlighted path includes the RF matching network as a functional group.
J12.name: Sub-GHz antenna

J18.description: Small I²C expansion connector compatible with Qwiic and STEMMA QT devices. It uses MCU_I2C0 and supplies 3.3 V.
J18.name: Qwiic connector

J24.description: Wired network connector. Signals pass through integrated magnetics to the RTL8211F PHY before reaching the processor.
J24.name: Gigabit Ethernet port

J2.description: Single-pair Ethernet connection with power over the data line. The board documentation specifies a 5 V, 250 mA output; this port is not the board’s power input.
J2.name: Single-pair Ethernet port

J10.description: Holds a CR1220 backup cell for the real-time clock. It does not power the main processor or charge a battery.
J10.name: RTC battery holder

J21.description: Accepts compatible Click boards. Select an individual contact below to trace its function. Bus assignment depends on the operating-system pin configuration.
J21.name: mikroBUS socket

SH1.description: A separate wireless MCU for BLE and sub-GHz networking. Linux communicates with its firmware over UART6. Radio capabilities depend on the loaded firmware.
SH1.name: BeaglePlay shielding cover
SH1.specification: BeaglePlay shielding cover; 0.2mm thick white copper, 21.4*16.9*1.7mm, A.5 (design)
